newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran South Pars reserves could be revised up - MEE.
newsitem.headline: Iran South Pars reserves could be revised up - MEE.

text.p: The National Iranian Oil Co's (NIOC) offshore arm expects to revise upward estimates of the South Pars gas field's reserves to perhaps as much as 500 trillion cubic feet, the Middle East Economic Survey reported on Monday.
It said recently-completed studies of the field had allowed NIOC to lift its reserve estimates for South Pars to over 300 trillion cubic feet from 128 trillion cubic feet.

"There are strong indications, however, that this figure could be revised upward even further, possibly as high as 500 trillion cubic feet according to Mr Jalilian," MEES said in a report of an interview with NIOC offshore director Seyed Jalilian.
South Pars is an extension in Iranian waters of Qatar's North Field.

"Up until recently it was assumed that over two-thirds of the field was located on the Qatari side of the border. But the new revisions -- if they are borne out -- would make the overall South Pars/North field structure more of an Iranian reservoir than a Qatari one," MEES said.
MEES said the NIOC division had in the past two years increased offshore oil production by 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 550,000 bpd.
The increase was achieved despite U.S. sanctions, which it said had presented some challenges for the industry.

"Jalilian reckons that problems securing essential spare parts and maintenance assistance from an American manufacturer of gas turbines has temporarily inhibited production at one offshore field by an estimated 25,000 bpd," MEES said.
It said NIOC hoped to award "at least one" of the schemes for the development of the Balal, Soroush and Doroud fields by the end of the current Iranian year in March 1997.
